questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted a college that had lots of school spirit and great education. At the same time I wanted to live somewhere unlike what I have tried before.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved every second of it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UT is very helpful, so it was fairly easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Assistance from the international department at UT

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: If you are only in Texas for a semester, it can be difficult to find housing where a half-year lease is available. I signed an apartment though UT but off-campus for a whole year and then applied to break the contract after the semester, which was possible because I was an exchange student. I can recommend 2400 Nueces apartments through UT.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: A lot of exchange students will live at the co-op. They are very "kollegie" like and can be fun but I know that a lot of my friends didn't love it because the facilities aren't super good, its not very clean and when you live there you have responsibilities like cooking and cleaning as well as common dining.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Its all done in the same portal that you use for information before arrival. Upload DS-2019 and and proof of entering the states when you arrive.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: All student services at UT are just great and extremely helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted. There are many classes that have pre-requisits, so make sure that any bars are lifted for the classes you want before registration opens. If you have any trouble, e-mail or call the department that has the class - they are very helpful, especially towards exchange students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check out the course schedule to make sure the classes you want don't overlap and that your schedule is as you would like for it to be. Be ready when it opens, sign up for waitlists if you don't get the class and generally have extra backup classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All the courses I took had a good level

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I really like the level of the courses, especially game theory (micro III) was pretty advanced and like I would expect it to be in Denmark.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Tennis, Lacrosse, sorority

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Find a club or a sport that you wanna do, this is such a good way to make friends. In the beginning of the semester there is an event called "Party on Plaza" where all the orgs are tabling, so go there and find something you want to be a part of.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I travelled a bit in the US and otherwise I just had fun with my friends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join something

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Students are a bit younger, so the age-gap can be a little obvious sometimes, but its not too bad.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The hospitality

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Socialize with locals and not just exchange students, go to the games, enjoy the university atmosphere on campus

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy your semester!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I gained so many friendships

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Managing all the little details, bills, registrations etc. on your own

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: UT is great and I would recommend everyone to go!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
